name: Malayalam

ancestors.notes: Descended from Old Tamil; split c. 9th century CE
Very heavy Sanskrit adstrate: ~50% of formal vocabulary

notes: Standard Malayalam (Kerala). Descended from Old Tamil, diverged c. 9th–13th century CE. Unique phoneme: ⟨ഴ⟩ = /z/ (derived from Proto-Dravidian *ḻ, retained as /z/ only in Malayalam). Uses the most complex Brahmic script (~60 base characters). Phonemic gemination. Heavy Sanskrit vocabulary in formal register.

allophone_rules.notes: Malayalam inherits the Dravidian intervocalic/post-nasal voicing rules from its parent (ta): plosives are voiceless word-initially and when geminated, voiced between vowels and after a nasal (Asher & Kumari 1997: 405-406; Krishnamurti 2003: 4.2) — പകർച്ച [paɡar-], മരുതം [marud̪am]. It differs from Tamil in ONE realisation: the palatal ⟨ച⟩ does not lenite to [s] between vowels, it voices to [dʑ] like the rest of the series (Asher & Kumari 1997: 405-406). These rules override the inherited TA_VOICE_tɕ* by id.

Malayalam-specific override of ta's TA_GEM1_r/TA_GEM2_r. Unlike Tamil, where a doubled rhotic letter is a phonetically long trill, Malayalam's written ⟨റ്റ⟩ (റ + virama + റ) represents a single phoneme realised as a voiceless ALVEOLAR stop, contrasting with the dental geminate stop spelled ⟨ത്ത⟩. Proto-Dravidian *ṯṯ was retained as a stop while the singleton *ṯ lenited to the trill /r/ (Krishnamurti 2003). Asher & Kumari (1997: 432-435), as reported in Namboodiripad & Garellek (2017: 113-114, Journal of the IPA 47(1)): 'the geminate /tː/ ... /patːi/ "was able to"' — a plain (non-dental) /tː/, distinct from the /t̪ː/ row for the ⟨ത്ത⟩ series. The first half carries the length; the second half is stripped to its bare vowel, same C+C+V -> Cː+V mechanics as the inherited TA_GEM pattern. HAZARD FOR ta AUDITORS: ml overrides this rule by id (TA_GEM1_r / TA_GEM2_r) and additionally depends on ta having no existing id 'TA_GEM2_r_FINAL'. Renaming or restructuring ta's TA_GEM1_r/TA_GEM2_r in a future ta audit silently reverts Malayalam to a long trill /rː/ for ⟨റ്റ⟩ instead of the correct /tː/ stop, with no test failure in ta's own suite — the leak only shows up in ml's test_indic_allophony.py.

Malayalam-specific companion to TA_GEM2_r: closes the word. The inherited rule only strips the geminate's second half when a vowel follows in the SAME syllable slot (Tamil put̪ːakam-style); a written ⟨റ്റ⟩ that is itself the last thing in the word — no vowel sign, closed instead by a word-final virama and the samvrutokaram vowel virama_final_vowel supplies afterwards — has no such following vowel to carry, so it needs its own word-final variant of the same second-half deletion. See TA_GEM1_r for the citation (Asher & Kumari 1997: 432-435; Namboodiripad & Garellek 2017: 113-114). Own id (not shared with ta), but its preceded_by_phoneme=['r'] condition assumes ta's TA_GEM1_r still emits bare 'r' at that point — see the hazard note on TA_GEM1_r/TA_GEM2_r.
